evidence.note: Diagnosed that simple topology failed, tried external orthology (HomoloGene) as a different signal; got S3≈0.013 and abandoned it, then diagnosed random annealing as ineffective and pivoted to greedy construction.
Explicitly reasoned 'at current Ea even perfect E2 wouldn't reach 0.32; need to increase Ea', pivoting from replacement to swap-based search and then to downloading an established aligner (SANA).

Recognized the hot-temperature SANA run was collapsing the score (~0.09) and repeatedly tried to abort it, protecting the accumulated best (backed up as best234) rather than letting a bad run overwrite gains.

Formed the hypothesis that EC-weighted SANA reaches higher-Ea basins, then S3 improvers cut E2; ran a deliberate sweep of mixed EC/S3 weights, each followed by local improvers, keeping only improvements — though this later became somewhat repetitive grinding still short of 0.32.

For yeast, diagnosed the NC-vs-S3 tradeoff (perfect seed NC=1/S3=0.248 vs SANA S3=0.557/NC=0.169) and pivoted to a reference-seeded hybridizer to satisfy both constraints, iterating from a slow Python version to a faster C++ one.

reasoning: The agent repeatedly forms hypotheses about why a metric lags (Ea too low for S3; NC vs S3 tradeoff for yeast), tests targeted changes, combines complementary signals (orthology, topology/SANA, reference-seeding, hybridization) tuned to the two different constraint sets, and abandons dead ends quickly while preserving accumulated gains via systematic backups — matching the level-10 description of fluid, evidence-driven course-correction. It falls just short of a perfect 10 because the DM-HS mixed-weight sweep became a somewhat repetitive parameter grind that never escaped its plateau, so I place it at 9.
